parole.testo: Borrowed from Medieval Latin antilops, itself borrowed from Byzantine Greek ἀνθόλοψ (anthólops).

parole.significato: archaeologist (someone who is skilled, professes or practices archaeology)
parole.testo: From post-classical Latin archaiologus or its etymon Byzantine Greek ἀρχαιολόγος (arkhaiológos), from Ancient Greek ἀρχαιο- (arkhaio-) + -λογος (-logos). By surface analysis, archéologie + -logue.

Learned borrowing from Latin arsenicum, from Late/Byzantine Greek ἀρσενικόν (arsenikón, “yellow arsenic”), from Classical Syriac ܙܪܢܝܟܐ (zarnīḵā), from Middle Persian *zarnīk, from Old Median *zaraniyakā, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃-.
From Medieval Latin Basilidiānus, from Byzantine Greek Βασιλειδῐᾱνός (Basileidĭānós). By surface analysis, Basilide + -ien.

parole.significato: sandalwood (any of various trees in genus Santalum; the aromatic wood of such trees)
parole.testo: From Medieval Latin santalum, sandalum, from Byzantine Greek σάνταλον (sántalon), from Arabic صَنْدَل (ṣandal).
Inherited from Middle French Sclave, from Medieval Latin Sclavus, from Byzantine Greek Σκλάβος (Sklábos), which see for more. Doublet of esclave.

parole.significato: to stigmatize (to mark with a permanent identity mark branded, cut or tattooed onto the skin)
parole.testo: From Medieval Latin stigmatizō, from Byzantine Greek στιγματίζω (stigmatízō). By surface analysis, stigmate + -iser.
